questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Between you and I, / the proposal / is unlikely to be approved.
questions.x: The error is in part (a): 'Between you and I'. After the preposition 'between', use 'me': 'between you and me'.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
It is high time we (leave) for the station.
questions.x: Correct answer: left. 'It is high time' is followed by the past tense.

questions.q: In the sentence 'His laconic reply — "Noted." — irritated the committee', the word 'laconic' means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Using very few words. Laconic: brief, using few words.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
Scarcely had the auditor left the room (when the files went missing).
questions.x: 'Scarcely … when' is the correct pairing; 'than' goes with 'no sooner'.

questions.q: The court held the order to be ____, as the officer had no power to issue it.
questions.x: Ultra vires: beyond legal power.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The grant is a drop in the ocean compared with what the region needs', the idiom means:
o: Too small to make a real difference
questions.x: Correct answer: Too small to make a real difference. It describes an insignificant amount.

questions.q:
Rearrange the following sentences (P, Q, R, S) to form a coherent paragraph:
P: The first is to measure the water regularly.
Q: Managing a shared aquifer requires three steps.
R: The third is to agree on limits that every user respects.
S: The second is to share the data openly with all users.
questions.x: Correct answer: QPSR. Q announces three steps, followed by first, second and third.

questions.q: The sentence 'If water is heated to 100 °C at sea level, it boils' expresses:
questions.x: Correct answer: A general truth (zero conditional). Zero conditionals use the present in both clauses for facts.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
Unless you (do not submit) the form by Friday, your claim will be delayed.
questions.x: Correct answer: submit. 'Unless' already means 'if not'; a second negative is wrong.

questions.q: Part-time staff receive leave on a ____ basis, in proportion to the hours they work.
questions.x: Pro rata: proportionately.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The board has appointed / a committee comprising of / three senior officers.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'a committee comprising of'. 'Comprise' takes no 'of': 'comprising three officers'.

questions.q: Nobody called while I was out, ____?
questions.x: 'Nobody' is negative, so the tag is positive; 'they' refers to 'nobody'.

questions.q: The new scheme is aimed ____ helping small traders get credit.
questions.x: 'Aimed at' is the correct collocation.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, "I visited the plant yesterday."
o: She said that she had visited the plant the next day.
She said that she visited the plant yesterday.
She said that she had visited the plant the day before.
She said that she has visited the plant the previous day.
questions.x: Past simple becomes past perfect; 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'.

questions.q: The example of bank tellers is used to show that:
o: Automation often changes the content of a job rather than abolishing it
Banks prefer human workers to machines
All jobs are safe from automation
Cash machines failed to work properly
questions.x: Answer: 'Automation often changes the content of a job rather than abolishing it'. Tellers' work 'shifted towards advice and sales'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Predictions that machines will 'replace' whole occupations usually miss how work is organised. A job is a bundle of tasks, some routine and some requiring judgement, persuasion or care. Automation tends to remove tasks rather than entire jobs, and the remaining tasks often become more valuable. Bank tellers did not vanish when cash machines arrived; their work shifted towards advice and sales. The real risk is not mass unemployment overnight but a slow sorting in which workers who cannot move to the new tasks are left behind.

questions.q: According to the author, the main danger of automation is:
o: Machines becoming more expensive than workers
Workers who cannot adapt to new tasks being left behind
questions.x: Answer: 'Workers who cannot adapt to new tasks being left behind'. The 'real risk' is a 'slow sorting'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Predictions that machines will 'replace' whole occupations usually miss how work is organised. A job is a bundle of tasks, some routine and some requiring judgement, persuasion or care. Automation tends to remove tasks rather than entire jobs, and the remaining tasks often become more valuable. Bank tellers did not vanish when cash machines arrived; their work shifted towards advice and sales. The real risk is not mass unemployment overnight but a slow sorting in which workers who cannot move to the new tasks are left behind.

questions.q: Which policy follows most logically from the passage?
o: A ban on all new automation technology
Investment in retraining workers for tasks needing judgement and care
Reducing wages of workers in routine jobs
questions.x: Answer: 'Investment in retraining workers for tasks needing judgement and care'. If the risk is failure to move to new tasks, retraining addresses it. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Predictions that machines will 'replace' whole occupations usually miss how work is organised. A job is a bundle of tasks, some routine and some requiring judgement, persuasion or care. Automation tends to remove tasks rather than entire jobs, and the remaining tasks often become more valuable. Bank tellers did not vanish when cash machines arrived; their work shifted towards advice and sales. The real risk is not mass unemployment overnight but a slow sorting in which workers who cannot move to the new tasks are left behind.

questions.q: The central argument of the passage is that social security rights should:
o: Be provided only by large employers
Be paid as lump sums at each job change
Follow the individual worker across jobs
Be limited to workers with lifelong employment
questions.x: Answer: 'Follow the individual worker across jobs'. The last sentence says the worker, not the workplace, should be the unit to which rights attach. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: A worker who changes jobs four times in ten years should not have to rebuild her social security from scratch each time. Yet that is what happens when benefits are tied to a single employer rather than to the person. Portability is not a technical detail; it decides whether years of contribution add up to a pension or scatter into forgotten accounts. The more fluid the labour market becomes, the more a system designed for lifelong employment with one firm begins to leak. Reform, therefore, must begin by treating the worker, not the workplace, as the unit to which rights attach.

questions.q: The word 'leak', as used in the passage, suggests that the existing system:
o: Loses value that workers have built up when they move
questions.x: Answer: 'Loses value that workers have built up when they move'. Contributions 'scatter into forgotten accounts' — value is lost. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: A worker who changes jobs four times in ten years should not have to rebuild her social security from scratch each time. Yet that is what happens when benefits are tied to a single employer rather than to the person. Portability is not a technical detail; it decides whether years of contribution add up to a pension or scatter into forgotten accounts. The more fluid the labour market becomes, the more a system designed for lifelong employment with one firm begins to leak. Reform, therefore, must begin by treating the worker, not the workplace, as the unit to which rights attach.

questions.q: Which assumption underlies the author's argument?
o: Pensions are unnecessary for mobile workers
Job changes are becoming more frequent
questions.x: Answer: 'Job changes are becoming more frequent'. The argument depends on the labour market becoming 'more fluid'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: A worker who changes jobs four times in ten years should not have to rebuild her social security from scratch each time. Yet that is what happens when benefits are tied to a single employer rather than to the person. Portability is not a technical detail; it decides whether years of contribution add up to a pension or scatter into forgotten accounts. The more fluid the labour market becomes, the more a system designed for lifelong employment with one firm begins to leak. Reform, therefore, must begin by treating the worker, not the workplace, as the unit to which rights attach.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Deccan Riots of 1875:
1. They were directed mainly against moneylenders.
2. Peasants seized and destroyed debt bonds and deeds.
3. They led to the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Gandhara art shows strong Greco-Roman influence.
Reason (R): Gandhara lay on trade routes connecting India with the Hellenistic world.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Bhakti movement used regional languages extensively.
Reason (R): Bhakti saints sought to reach ordinary people beyond the elite who knew Sanskrit.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946):
1. It proposed a Union of India dealing with defence, foreign affairs and communications.
2. It provided for grouping of provinces into three sections.
3. It accepted the demand for a separate sovereign Pakistan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It rejected a separate Pakistan.

questions.q: Which leader is correctly matched with a newspaper he edited or founded?
questions.x: Correct answer: Bal Gangadhar Tilak — Kesari. Al-Hilal was Azad's; Young India Gandhi's; New India Besant's.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Swadeshi enterprises:
1. Prafulla Chandra Ray founded Bengal Chemicals.
2. V. O. Chidambaram Pillai started the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company.
3. The Tata Iron and Steel Company was set up by the Government of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
TISCO was founded in 1907 by the Tata group as a private Indian enterprise.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Bhimbetka:
1. It is a group of rock shelters in Madhya Pradesh with prehistoric paintings.
2. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
3. Its paintings depict hunting, dancing and animals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct; it was inscribed in 2003.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Civil Disobedience Movement:
1. It began with the Dandi March in March 1930.
2. Khudai Khidmatgars took part in the North-West Frontier Province.
3. The Congress attended the First Round Table Conference.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Congress boycotted the First RTC and attended only the Second.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. It introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
2. It made the central legislature bicameral.
3. It provided for direct elections on universal adult franchise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Franchise was limited by property and education.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Gandhi–Irwin Pact (March 1931):
1. The Congress agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement.
2. Political prisoners not convicted of violence were to be released.
3. The government agreed to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his associates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The pact did not secure commutation; they were executed on 23 March 1931.

questions.q:
Consider the following rivers:
1. Ravi
2. Jhelum
3. Beas
4. Chenab
Under the Indus Waters Treaty, how many of the above are 'eastern rivers'?
questions.x:
2 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Ravi and Beas are eastern rivers; Jhelum and Chenab are western rivers.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Mission Karmayogi:
1. It aims at capacity building of civil servants.
2. It is delivered through the iGOT Karmayogi digital platform.
3. It is run by the Union Public Service Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is overseen by the Capacity Building Commission and Karmayogi Bharat, an SPV.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana:
1. Loans are provided under Shishu, Kishore, Tarun and Tarun Plus categories.
2. Tarun Plus allows loans up to ₹20 lakh.
3. MUDRA loans require collateral above ₹50,000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
MUDRA loans are collateral-free.

questions.q:
Consider the following about COP30:
1. It was held at Belém, Brazil, in November 2025.
2. Belém is located at the edge of the Amazon rainforest.
3. It was the first UNFCCC COP ever held in Latin America.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Latin America had hosted earlier COPs — Buenos Aires (COP4, COP10), Mexico's Cancún (COP16) and Lima (COP20).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the papal election of 2025:
1. It followed the death of Pope Francis.
2. The new Pope, Leo XIV, is the first Pope from the United States.
3. The Pope is elected by all the bishops of the Catholic Church.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Pope is elected by the College of Cardinals (those under 80) in a conclave.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in 2025:
1. It was carried out by the Election Commission of India first in Bihar.
2. It was later extended to several other States and Union Territories.
3. It was conducted under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Preparation and revision of electoral rolls is under the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

questions.q:
Consider the following about semiconductor projects under the India Semiconductor Mission:
1. Micron's assembly and test plant is at Sanand, Gujarat.
2. Tata Electronics is setting up a fabrication unit at Dholera with PSMC of Taiwan.
3. All approved units are front-end fabs producing wafers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Most approved units are assembly, testing, marking and packaging (ATMP/OSAT) units.

questions.q:
Consider the following announcements of the Union Budget 2025-26:
1. No income tax is payable under the new regime on income up to ₹12 lakh, owing to an enhanced rebate.
2. The FDI limit for insurance companies was proposed to be raised from 74% to 100%, for companies investing the entire premium in India.
3. The fiscal deficit target for 2025-26 was set at 4.4% of GDP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
From 2026-27, debt-to-GDP was to serve as the fiscal anchor.

questions.q:
Consider the following developments of 2025:
1. The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025.
2. The Employment Linked Incentive scheme was launched as the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana.
3. ESIC ran SPREE 2025 to promote registration of employers and employees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three took place in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Semicon India 2025:
1. The Vikram 32-bit processor developed by ISRO's Semi-Conductor Laboratory was presented.
2. It was held in New Delhi.
3. It marked the start of mass production of 3-nm chips in an Indian fab.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India's first commercial fabs were still under construction and target mature nodes.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of a body and the authority appointing its head is correct?
o: Lokpal Chairperson — Lok Sabha Speaker alone
Chief Information Commissioner — Chief Justice of India
Central Vigilance Commissioner — President, on recommendation of a committee headed by the Prime Minister
questions.x: CVC, CIC, Lokpal and NHRC heads are appointed by the President on recommendations of high-level committees.

questions.q:
Match the parliamentary committee with its main function:
Committee:
A. Estimates Committee
B. Public Accounts Committee
C. Committee on Public Undertakings
D. Business Advisory Committee
Function:
1. Allots time for government and other business in the House
2. Examines CAG reports on appropriation and finance accounts
3. Examines reports and accounts of public sector undertakings
4. Suggests economies in the estimates; all members from the Lok Sabha
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Estimates Committee) → 4 (Suggests economies in the estimates; all members from the Lok Sabha); B (Public Accounts Committee) → 2 (Examines CAG reports on appropriation and finance accounts); C (Committee on Public Undertakings) → 3 (Examines reports and accounts of public sector undertakings); D (Business Advisory Committee) → 1 (Allots time for government and other business in the House).
The PAC and COPU each have 22 members (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha) but different mandates.

questions.q:
Who among the following participate in the election of the President of India?
1. Elected members of the Rajya Sabha
2. Nominated members of the Lok Sabha
3. Elected members of the Legislative Assembly of Puducherry
4. Elected members of State Legislative Councils
How many of the above participate?
questions.x:
2 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Elected MPs and elected MLAs (including Delhi and Puducherry) vote; nominated members and MLCs do not.

questions.q: A State refuses to comply with a Union direction under Article 256. Which consequence is provided by the Constitution?
o: The President may hold that the constitutional machinery has failed (Article 365), enabling Article 356
The State loses its seats in the Rajya Sabha
The Union can stop all tax devolution
The Supreme Court automatically dissolves the State Assembly
questions.x: Correct answer: The President may hold that the constitutional machinery has failed (Article 365), enabling Article 356. Article 365 links non-compliance with directions to Article 356.

questions.q:
With reference to Article 32, consider the following:
1. It is itself a Fundamental Right.
2. The Supreme Court can issue writs only for enforcement of Fundamental Rights under it.
3. Parliament can empower any other court to issue writs within its jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Article 32(3) allows Parliament to empower other courts.

questions.q:
Consider the following about writs:
1. Habeas corpus can be issued against private individuals as well as the State.
2. Mandamus cannot be issued against the President or a Governor.
3. Certiorari can be issued against a private company.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Certiorari lies against judicial and quasi-judicial authorities, and is not available against private bodies.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Constituent Assembly:
1. Its members were indirectly elected by the members of the provincial legislative assemblies.
2. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the President of the Constituent Assembly.
3. It also functioned as the first Parliament of free India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was its President; Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

questions.q: Parliament wants to legislate on a State subject for two States that have requested it by resolutions. The relevant Article is:
questions.x: Article 252: legislation by consent of two or more States, which other States may adopt.

questions.q: Which of the following requires a 'special majority' of Parliament under Article 368 AND ratification by at least half the State legislatures?
o: An amendment changing the representation of States in Parliament
questions.x: Federal provisions (e.g., representation of States, election of President, Seventh Schedule) need ratification; creation of a new State is by simple majority under Articles 2–4.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the procedure under Article 368:
1. An amendment Bill may be introduced in either House of Parliament.
2. The President must give assent to an amendment Bill duly passed.
3. A Bill affecting federal provisions must be ratified by the legislatures of all States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Ratification by at least half of the States is required; the 24th Amendment made assent obligatory.

questions.q:
Consider the following about urban local bodies under the 74th Amendment:
1. Ward Committees are required in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more.
2. The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functions.
3. Metropolitan Planning Committees are required in metropolitan areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about citizenship:
1. India does not permit dual citizenship.
2. OCI cardholders cannot vote in elections.
3. Citizenship is a subject of the Union List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Entry 17 of the Union List covers citizenship.

questions.q:
Which of the following have been recognised by the Supreme Court as part of Article 21?
1. Right to privacy
2. Right to livelihood
3. Right to a speedy trial
4. Right to strike
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
There is no fundamental right to strike.

questions.q: A government's revenue receipts are ₹34 lakh crore, non-debt capital receipts ₹0.8 lakh crore, revenue expenditure ₹39 lakh crore and capital expenditure ₹11 lakh crore. The revenue deficit and fiscal deficit are respectively:
questions.x: Correct answer: ₹5 lakh crore and ₹15.2 lakh crore. RD = 39 − 34 = 5; FD = (39 + 11) − (34 + 0.8) = 15.2.

questions.q: Budget data (₹ crore): Revenue receipts 28,000; Non-debt capital receipts 4,000; Revenue expenditure 50,000 (of which interest payments 8,000); Capital expenditure 8,000. The primary deficit is:
questions.x:
Total expenditure = 50,000 + 8,000 = 58,000.
Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts) = 58,000 − 32,000 = 26,000.
Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest = 18,000.
Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts = 22,000.
Answer (primary): ₹18,000 crore.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Large fiscal deficits can crowd out private investment.
Reason (R): Government borrowing raises demand for loanable funds and pushes up interest rates.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: Under the revised MSME criteria (Budget 2025–26), an enterprise with plant and machinery investment of ₹20 crore and turnover of ₹120 crore is classified as:
questions.x: Small requires investment ≤ ₹25 crore AND turnover ≤ ₹100 crore; turnover exceeds ₹100 crore, so it is medium (≤ ₹125 crore investment, ≤ ₹500 crore turnover).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the monetary policy framework in India:
1. The inflation target is set by the Government in consultation with the RBI.
2. The Monetary Policy Committee has three members from the RBI and three external members.
3. The RBI Governor has a casting vote in case of a tie.
4. The target is wholesale price inflation of 4%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct; Statement 4 is incorrect.
The target is CPI (combined) inflation of 4% with a ±2% band.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the public finances of the Union:
1. No money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except under appropriation made by law.
2. The Contingency Fund is placed at the disposal of the President to meet unforeseen expenditure.
3. Provident fund deposits of government employees are credited to the Public Account.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Articles 266 and 267; GPF and small savings go to the Public Account.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹3,70,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 3,70,000 × (0.8)^3 = ₹1,89,440.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹1,48,000.)

questions.q: A firm earns an average profit of ₹1,54,500 on capital employed of ₹9,30,000. The normal rate of return in the industry is 15%. Goodwill at 4 years' purchase of super profit is:

Consider the following items:
1. Wages paid for installing a new machine
2. Repairs to an existing building
3. Legal fees paid for acquiring land
4. Insurance premium on the factory
How many of the above are capital expenditure?
questions.x:
2 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Installation wages and legal fees on acquisition are capitalised.

questions.q: A suspense account was opened with a credit of ₹1,000. Later it was found that the purchases book was overcast by ₹1,000. The rectifying entry is:
o: Purchases A/c Dr. To Suspense A/c ₹1,000
Creditors A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c ₹1,000
Suspense A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c ₹1,000
Suspense A/c Dr. To Creditors A/c ₹1,000
questions.x: Overcasting the purchases book made Purchases debit excessive; crediting Purchases and debiting Suspense closes the suspense balance.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹20,000; Purchases ₹2,55,000; Purchase returns ₹2,000; Carriage inwards ₹4,000; Sales ₹2,42,000; Sales returns ₹1,000; Closing stock ₹70,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 20,000 + 2,55,000 − 2,000 + 4,000 − 70,000 = ₹2,07,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 2,42,000 − 1,000 − 2,07,000 = ₹34,000.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: A cheque of ₹5,000 received from Arun and deposited was dishonoured; bank charged ₹100. The entry in the payee's books is:
o: Arun A/c Dr. ₹5,100 To Bank A/c ₹5,100
Bank A/c Dr. ₹5,100 To Arun A/c ₹5,100
Arun A/c Dr. ₹5,000; Bank charges A/c Dr. ₹100 To Bank A/c ₹5,100
Bad debts A/c Dr. To Bank A/c ₹5,100
questions.x: Bank charges caused by the dishonour are recoverable from Arun, so Arun is debited with ₹5,100.

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹50,000, Debtors ₹70,000, Inventory ₹1,00,000, Prepaid expenses ₹10,000, Creditors ₹40,000, Bills payable ₹7,500 and Outstanding expenses ₹7,500. Its current ratio is:

Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A capital account with a debit balance indicates that the proprietor's drawings and losses exceed capital and profits.
Reason (R): Capital account normally shows a credit balance as it represents the owner's claim on the business.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. A debit balance arises when the owner's claim becomes negative.

questions.q: After a fire, an insured trader makes no effort to save goods that could easily have been moved. The insurer can reduce the claim because the trader violated the principle of:
questions.x: The insured must act as a prudent uninsured person and take reasonable steps to minimise loss.

questions.q: P/V ratio is 40% and fixed costs are ₹2,00,000. Sales required to earn a profit of ₹60,000 are:
questions.x: (Fixed cost + profit) / P/V ratio = 2,60,000 / 0.40 = ₹6,50,000.

questions.q:
Consider the following about B. Shah v. Presiding Officer, Labour Court (1977):
1. It concerned computation of maternity benefit.
2. It held that the benefit is payable for all days of the period, including Sundays.
3. It held that maternity benefit is payable only to permanent employees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The judgment favoured a liberal computation; it did not restrict benefit to permanent employees.

questions.q: A contractor engages 55 workers to work in two establishments located in different States for a single principal employer project. Under the OSH Code, the contractor:
o: Is exempt because no single site has 50 workers
Needs separate licences for each work order
Needs no licence because the principal employer is registered
Can obtain a single licence covering work in more than one State
questions.x: The OSH Code allows a single licence for work in more than one State or the whole country.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Code on Wages limits excluded components to half of total remuneration while computing 'wages'.
Reason (R): Employers had often inflated allowances to depress basic wages on which provident fund, gratuity and bonus are computed.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The 50% rule in Section 2(y) is designed precisely to curb wage-splitting that reduced social security contributions.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Unemployment measured by Current Weekly Status is usually higher than by usual status.
Reason (R): CWS captures short-term unemployment in the reference week that usual status (365 days) may not.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Shorter reference periods pick up spells of unemployment that the longer usual status smooths out.

questions.q: A factory pays monthly wages. For the month of June, the salary is credited on 9 July. A worker complains. Under the Code on Wages, which of the following is correct?
o: Payment is in time because only daily-rated workers have a deadline
Payment is in time because the Code allows ten days for establishments with over 1,000 workers
Payment is late; monthly wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the following month
The deadline is the 15th of the following month for all employers
questions.x: The old Payment of Wages Act gave 10 days to establishments with more than 1,000 workers; the Code on Wages has a uniform rule — before the end of the 7th day of the succeeding month.

questions.q: A company has 9 employees, all men, at its head office. A woman consultant visiting the office complains of sexual harassment by an employee. Where should the complaint go?
o: The National Commission for Women only
The Local Committee constituted by the District Officer
questions.x: Workplaces with fewer than 10 employees need not constitute an Internal Committee.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A fixed-term worker under the IR Code gets the same wages and benefits as a permanent worker doing similar work.
Reason (R): Fixed-term employment is a contract that ends automatically on expiry of the term without notice.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true. R describes how fixed-term contracts end, but parity of wages arises from the statutory mandate, not from the manner of termination.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Fine-only offences under the Labour Codes can be compounded.
Reason (R): Compounding allows first-time minor violations to be settled by paying a sum instead of facing prosecution.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Compounding is meant to decriminalise minor first offences.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes 'lay-off' from 'retrenchment' under the IR Code?
o: Lay-off is a temporary inability to give work with the worker on the rolls; retrenchment ends the employment for reasons other than punishment
questions.x: Correct answer: Lay-off is a temporary inability to give work with the worker on the rolls; retrenchment ends the employment for reasons other than punishment. Lay-off is temporary (shortage of material, power, breakdown, etc.).

questions.q: An employee who discovers that a colleague with similar output is paid more becomes demotivated and reduces effort. This is best explained by:
questions.x: Adams' equity theory: perceived inequity of input–outcome ratios.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The OSH Code mandates an appointment letter to every employee.
Reason (R): Written terms of employment help workers prove their status and claim social security benefits.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Formalisation through appointment letters is the stated rationale.

questions.q: Under the ID Act, 1947, which industry could be declared a 'public utility service' by the appropriate government for a limited period?
o: An industry listed in the First Schedule, such as banking or cement
Any industry with more than 100 workers
questions.x: Industries in the First Schedule could be declared public utility services for up to six months at a time, extendable.

questions.q: The Labour Bureau's CPI-IW is used for revising dearness allowance. Which feature of the 2016 series is correct?
o: It uses 2012 as base and covers rural labourers
It is compiled by the NSO
It has a base year of 2016 = 100 and wider coverage of centres than the 2001 series
questions.x: Correct answer: It has a base year of 2016 = 100 and wider coverage of centres than the 2001 series. The 2016 series covers 88 centres (78 earlier) and includes housing.

questions.q:
With reference to the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, consider the following:
1. It applied to establishments employing twenty or more contract workers.
2. Abolition of contract labour in a process depended on factors such as whether the work was perennial.
3. Abolition automatically made the contract workers regular employees of the principal employer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
SAIL (2001) held there is no automatic absorption on abolition.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The ILO's supervisory system includes the Committee on Freedom of Association.
Reason (R): The Committee can examine complaints even against countries that have not ratified the freedom of association conventions.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Membership of the ILO itself creates the obligation, which explains why the Committee exists alongside ratification-based supervision.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017:
1. Paid leave is 26 weeks for a woman with fewer than two surviving children.
2. A woman adopting a child below three months gets 12 weeks' leave.
3. A creche is mandatory for establishments with 10 or more employees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The creche requirement applies to establishments with 50 or more employees.

questions.q: An eligible employee earns ₹12,500 per month. The notified minimum wage for the employment is ₹6,500 per month. If the establishment declares bonus at 10%, the annual bonus payable is (statutory computation):
questions.x:
For computing bonus, salary is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher: max(7,000, 6,500) = ₹7,000.
Salary for computation = min(12,500, 7,000) = ₹7,000.
Annual bonus = 7,000 × 12 × 10% = ₹8,400. Bonus must lie between 8.33% and 20%.

questions.q: An employee whose average daily wage is ₹162 works in an ESI-covered factory and earns ₹12,500 in a month. Which statement about the month's contribution is correct?
o: Only the employer pays 3.25% (≈ ₹407); the employee's share is exempt
Neither pays, as low-wage employees are excluded from coverage
questions.x: Employees whose average daily wage is up to ₹176 are exempt from paying their own 0.75% share, but they remain covered and the employer must still pay 3.25% of wages. Here employer share ≈ ₹407.

questions.q:
Consider the following decisions of the CBT (EPF) in October 2025 on partial withdrawals:
1. Thirteen withdrawal provisions were merged into three categories.
2. Members may withdraw up to 100% of the eligible balance, but must keep 25% of contributions as minimum balance.
3. The minimum service for any partial withdrawal was raised to five years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Minimum service was made a uniform 12 months.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A member who defers EPS pension from 58 to 60 gets a higher pension.
Reason (R): EPS provides an increase of 4% for each year of deferment.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The 2016 amendment allows deferment up to 60 with a 4% annual increase.

questions.q: Which pair correctly contrasts the Bismarckian and Beveridgean models?
o: Bismarckian — contributory, employment-linked; Beveridgean — universal, flat-rate, tax-financed
questions.x: Correct answer: Bismarckian — contributory, employment-linked; Beveridgean — universal, flat-rate, tax-financed. Germany's 1880s social insurance vs the UK's 1942 Beveridge plan.

questions.q:
Consider the following about health insurance schemes:
1. The Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana was subsumed in PM-JAY.
2. Treatment under PM-JAY is cashless at empanelled hospitals.
3. Beneficiary families pay the premium under PM-JAY.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The premium is funded by the Centre and States.

questions.q: Which employee is NOT entitled to gratuity on leaving service?
o: The nominee of an employee who dies after 2 years of service
A permanent employee who resigns after 4 years and 2 months
An employee retiring on superannuation after 22 years
A fixed-term employee whose 18-month contract ends
questions.x: Resignation needs five years of continuous service (for permanent employees); fixed-term employees qualify after one year; death waives the condition.

questions.q: An EPF member in continuous service dies. Average monthly wages over the last 12 months were ₹5,000 and the average balance in the member's PF account over that period was ₹4,20,000. The assurance benefit under the EDLI Scheme is:
questions.x:
EDLI = 35 × average monthly wages (ceiling ₹15,000) + 50% of the average PF balance (bonus capped at ₹1,75,000), subject to a minimum of ₹2.5 lakh and a maximum of ₹7 lakh.
35 × 5,000 = ₹1,75,000; bonus = min(50% × 4,20,000, 1,75,000) = ₹1,75,000.
Total ₹3,50,000.

questions.q:
Consider the following about dark matter:
1. It does not emit or absorb light in any detectable way.
2. Its existence is inferred from gravitational effects such as galaxy rotation curves.
3. It is made of ordinary atoms of hydrogen and helium.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is not made of ordinary (baryonic) matter.

questions.q:
Consider the following about allotropes of carbon:
1. Graphite conducts electricity, while diamond does not.
2. Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice.
3. Fullerenes are made of carbon and hydrogen.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Fullerenes are made of carbon only.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the ozone layer:
1. It absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.
2. CFCs release chlorine that destroys ozone in the stratosphere.
3. The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol phases down HFCs, which are mainly a concern for ozone depletion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
HFCs do not deplete ozone; they are phased down because they are strong greenhouse gases.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Aditya-L1 is placed in a halo orbit around the Sun–Earth L1 point.
Reason (R): From L1 the Sun can be observed continuously without being hidden by the Earth.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. L1 lies about 1.5 million km from the Earth towards the Sun.

questions.q:
Consider the following about heat stress:
1. Wet-bulb temperature reflects both heat and humidity.
2. High humidity reduces the body's ability to cool by evaporation of sweat.
3. Heat stroke is milder than heat exhaustion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Heat stroke is a medical emergency; heat exhaustion is less severe.

questions.q: A traffic police radar gun measures the speed of a moving car. It works on:
o: The change in frequency of waves reflected from a moving object
Total internal reflection of radio waves
The change in the speed of light near a moving object
Interference of sound waves from the engine
questions.x: This is the Doppler effect, also used in echocardiography and weather radar.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Internet of Things (IoT):
1. It connects everyday devices with sensors to the internet.
2. Edge computing processes some data close to the device instead of in a distant cloud.
3. IoT devices cannot be targets of cyber-attacks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Weakly secured IoT devices are often hijacked into botnets.

questions.q:
Consider the following about logic gates:
1. NAND and NOR are called universal gates.
2. An XOR gate gives output 1 when its two inputs differ.
3. An AND gate gives output 1 if any one input is 1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
AND gives 1 only when all inputs are 1; that description fits OR.

questions.q:
Consider the following about databases:
1. A primary key must be unique and cannot be null.
2. A foreign key links a table to the primary key of another table.
3. SELECT is a Data Definition Language (DDL) command.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
SELECT is a query (DML/DQL) command; CREATE, ALTER and DROP are DDL.

questions.q:
Consider the following about India's nuclear power programme:
1. Pressurised heavy water reactors use natural uranium as fuel.
2. The second stage uses fast breeder reactors.
3. The third stage aims to use thorium, of which India has large reserves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
This is Homi Bhabha's three-stage plan.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Photochemical smog is described as oxidising.
Reason (R): It has high concentrations of oxidants such as ozone and nitrogen dioxide.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Classical smog, rich in SO₂, is reducing.

questions.q:
Consider the following about salt and blood pressure:
1. The WHO recommends that adults consume less than 5 g of salt a day.
2. High sodium intake raises the risk of hypertension.
3. Potassium-rich foods raise blood pressure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Potassium helps lower blood pressure.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Information Technology Act, 2000:
1. Section 66A was struck down by the Supreme Court in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015).
2. Section 69A empowers the Government to block public access to online information.
3. The Act does not recognise electronic signatures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Act gives legal recognition to electronic records and electronic signatures.

questions.q: ₹11,000 is invested for 1 year at 12% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly. The compound interest earned is:
questions.x:
Half-yearly: rate per period = 12/2 = 6%, number of periods = 2.
Amount = 11,000 × (1 + 6/100)² = ₹12,359.60.
CI = ₹1,359.60 (slightly more than annual compounding, which gives ₹1,320).

questions.q: In a certain code, 'A − B' means A is the daughter of B; 'A $ B' means A is the father of B; 'A + B' means A is the wife of B; 'A # B' means A is the brother of B. If 'K + R # T' (read as K + R and R # T), how is K related to T?
questions.x:
K + R: K is the wife of R. R # T: R is the brother of T.
Combining the two (all persons taken to be of one family, as is conventional): K is the sister-in-law of T.

questions.q: Two candles of the same length are lit at the same time. The first burns out completely in 7 hours and the second in 4 hours, each burning at a uniform rate. After how long will the first candle be exactly twice as long as the second?
questions.x:
After t hours the first candle has (1 − t/7) of its length left and the second (1 − t/4).
1 − t/7 = 2(1 − t/4) ⇒ t(2/4 − 1/7) = 1 ⇒ t = 7×4/(2×7 − 4) = 28/10 h = 2 h 48 min.

questions.q: In a row, Nisha is 14th from the left and Asif is 13th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Nisha becomes 29th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Nisha occupies Asif's old place, which is 13th from the right and now 29th from the left.
Total = 29 + 13 − 1 = 41.

questions.q: Find the next term in the series: I8L, M12P, Q20T, U32X, ?
questions.x:
First letters advance by 4 (I, M, Q, U, Y); the last letter is always 3 places after the first; the numbers increase by 4, 8, 12, … (8, 12, 20, 32, 48).
Next term: Y48B.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 5, 27, 14, 21, 23, 15, 32, ?
questions.x: Two interleaved series: odd positions 5, 14, 23, 32 (+9); even positions 27, 21, 15 (−6). The 8th term belongs to the even series: 15 − 6 = 9.

questions.q: The population of a hill town rises by 25%, then falls by 10%, and finally rises by 20%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 25/100) × (1 − 10/100) × (1 + 20/100) = 1.25 × 0.9 × 1.2 = 1.35.
Overall change = (1.35 − 1) × 100 = 35% → 35% increase.
Note: simply adding (25 − 10 + 20) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.

questions.q: On which day of the week did 10 April 1892 fall?
questions.x:
Odd-day method (Sunday = 0).
Completed years = 1891: 1600 years → 0 odd days; 200 years → 3; remaining 91 years have 22 leap + 69 ordinary → 22×2 + 69 = 113 → 1 odd day(s).
Days elapsed in 1892 up to 10 April = 101 → 3 odd day(s).
Total = 3 + 1 + 3 = 7 → 0 → Sunday.

questions.q: The monthly incomes of P and Q are in the ratio 5 : 4 and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 3 : 1. If each of them saves ₹15,750 a month, P's monthly income is:
questions.x:
Let incomes = 5k, 4k and expenditures = 3m, 1m.
5k − 3m = 4k − 1m = 15,750 → 1k = 2m.
Solving gives k = 4,500, m = 2,250.
P's income = 5 × 4,500 = ₹22,500 (check: ₹22,500 − ₹6,750 = ₹15,750).

questions.q: A vessel holds 100 litres of pure milk. 10 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.x:
After n replacements, milk = x(1 − y/x)ⁿ.
= 100 × (1 − 10/100)² = 100 × (0.9)² = 81 litres.
Removing 2 × 10 directly is wrong because the second draw removes a mixture, not pure milk.

questions.q: Farhan starts from point O and walks 7 km towards North, then turns left and walks 21 km, then turns left and walks 12 km, and finally turns left and walks 9 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: +7 -12 = -5 km → 5 km South.
East–West: -21 +9 = -12 km → 12 km West.
Distance = √(12² + 5²) = 13 km, towards South-West.

questions.q: One card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 playing cards. What is the probability that it is a red face card or a black ace?
questions.x:
Count the favourable cards, removing any overlap between the two conditions: 8 cards.
P = 8/52 = 2/13.

questions.q: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 1:51?
questions.x:
Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30×1 − 5.5×51| = |30 − 280.5| = 250.5°.
Since this exceeds 180°, the smaller angle = 360 − 250.5 = 109.5°.
(The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute over the hour hand.)

questions.q: Find the volume of a cylindrical water tank of radius 3.5 m and height 21 m. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.x:
V = πr²h = (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 × 21 = 808.5 m³.
(Curved surface 2πrh would be 462 m² — a common mix-up.)
